critical_steps: Both swapped families have energy \(2|x|^2+2a^2|y|^2\), so \(A=B=2\) are admissible \(K\)-frame bounds for \(K=P_{e_1}\).
The synthesis difference has exact norm \(2\sqrt2\,a\), and choosing \(\lambda=2\sqrt2\,a\) satisfies the proposition's smallness condition for every \(0<a\le1/8\).
The mixed weave containing two copies of \(e_1+a e_2\) annihilates \(-a e_1+e_2\), whose \(K^*\)-image is nonzero.
The source proof uses \(\|f\|\le\|K^\dagger\|\|K^*f\|\) outside \(R(K)\), where it need not hold.
If all atoms lie in \(R(K)\), projecting an arbitrary test vector into \(R(K)\) makes the source argument valid.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact one-parameter counterfamily on \(\mathbb C^2\), plus direct inspection of the proposition and proof.
integrity.unproved_limits: No minimal perturbation hypothesis or complete characterization of valid repairs is asserted.

scientific_limitations: The result refutes Proposition 3.3 as stated and provides a sufficient range-based repair.
The extra assumption that all atoms lie in \(R(K)\) is sufficient but is not claimed necessary.
More general repairs may instead impose perturbation control directly in the \(K^*\)-seminorm.
title: Arbitrarily small synthesis perturbations can satisfy Proposition 3.3 yet destroy \(K\)-wovenness
